saints.name: St. Theodosius the Cenobiarch
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: A father of communal monasticism whose great house near Bethlehem sheltered hundreds in the desert…
biography: Born in 423 at Mogarissus in Cappadocia, Theodosius set out for Jerusalem about the time of the Council of Chalcedon in 451, pausing to be blessed by Symeon on his pillar. He learned the monastic life under the hermit Longinus and then dwelt in a cave near Bethlehem, where disciples gathered around him.

His house grew into a great monastery, with churches where Greeks, Armenians, and Bessi each sang the office in their own tongue and hospitals for the sick, the aged, and the feeble in mind. When the patriarch Sallust set Sabas over the hermits of Palestine, he made Theodosius head of all who lived the common life; hence his title Cenobiarch, the chief of the cenobites.

A steadfast defender of Chalcedon, he withstood the Monophysite emperor Anastasius, who drove the aged abbot into exile; restored after the emperor's death, he died near Jerusalem in 529, being, by tradition, one hundred and five years old. His monastery above the road from Jerusalem to Bethlehem endured for centuries.
saints.knownFor: Organizing the common life of the desert monks of Palestine.
